nodes.description: PRKD1 phosphorylates class IIa histone deacetylases, promoting their nuclear export and derepressing MEF2- and TBX5-dependent transcription. Altered PRKD1 kinase activity dysregulates this axis, perturbing the transcriptional programs that control cardiac and ectodermal morphogenesis.

nodes.description: PRKD1 is essential for normal cardiac morphogenesis. Disrupted PRKD1 signaling impairs outflow tract and cardiac septum development, producing the conotruncal and septal congenital heart defects seen in CHDED. In the mouse, loss of Prkd1 causes complex structural heart defects and is lethal.

nodes.description: Disrupted PRKD1/HDAC-MEF2 transcriptional control is inferred to impair craniofacial and neural development, producing the dysmorphic facial features, microcephaly, developmental delay, and intellectual disability seen across the syndrome. nodes.description: Heterozygous PRKD1 variants alter the activity of protein kinase D1, a diacylglycerol/PKC-activated serine/threonine kinase. The recurrent de novo missense variants that characterize the dominant syndrome behave as gain-of-function alleles, while biallelic truncating variants (which cause a related recessive truncus arteriosus phenotype) and some heterozygous loss-of-function alleles reduce kinase function. Both perturbations disrupt PRKD1-dependent developmental signaling.

nodes.description: Persistent truncus arteriosus, a conotruncal defect, belongs to the related autosomal recessive phenotype caused by biallelic truncating PRKD1 variants, not to the dominant CHDED syndrome curated here. It is recorded because the two conditions share the PRKD1 outflow-tract mechanism; truncus arteriosus has not been reported in the heterozygous dominant syndrome.
